card.name: Nestinarstvo
card.era: Probable Thracian fire-cult roots; first documented 1862
card.tagline: Strandzha barefoot fire-dancing rite for Sts Constantine & Helena.
card.profile: A barefoot firewalking ritual with ecstatic dance, the climax of the Panagyr on the feast of Saints Constantine and Helena (3-4 June, Orthodox calendar) in the village of Bulgari in the Strandzha region of south-east Bulgaria. After a morning procession with sacred icons to a holy spring (with drum and bagpipe), the nestinari enter a trance and tread a ring of glowing embers carrying the icons, led by the sacred drum, to ensure the community's health and fertility (UNESCO; English Wikipedia).
card.insight: Inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List in 2009 (decision 4.COM 13.05; file RL/00191); it survives authentically chiefly in Bulgari, with related Greek 'Anastenaria' carried by refugees from Eastern Thrace after the 1912-13 Balkan Wars (UNESCO).
card.image_significance: Barefoot on living embers. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Strandzha (Bulgari), Bulgaria.
